record.paper_title: Five open problems in theory of quantum information
record.original_question: Explain whether the behavior of mutually unbiased measurements in coarse-grained or continuous-variable quantum systems is connected to the unresolved special role of discrete Hilbert-space dimension N=6. Continuous systems have at most three mutually unbiased bases, coarse-grained even-dimensional systems behave like continuous systems with no more than three mutually unbiased measurements, and it remains open whether this is related to the dimension-6 conundrum for discrete systems.

evidence.quote: While in the continuous case we maximally have3 MUBs [106], in the coarse-grained scenario [108] the situation is much more elaborate. Interestingly, the special dimension N = 6is not at all distinguished in the coarse-grained setting, since the systems of even dimension behave like the continuous ones (no more than 3 MUMs) — only odd dimensions nurture potential for more [108]. Whether this fact is connected to the conundrum ofN = 6 for discrete systems remains and open question at the moment.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

(a) Discrete setting. For a Hilbert space of dimension N, two orthonormal bases {|e_i⟩} and {|f_j⟩} are called mutually unbiased if |⟨e_i|f_j⟩|^2 = 1/N for all i,j. Let M(N) denote the maximum number of pairwise mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) in dimension N. It is known that M(N) ≤ N+1, with equality when N is a prime power. The value of M(6) is unknown; only M(6) ≥ 3 has been established, and it is widely conjectured but unproven that M(6) = 3. This is the so-called "dimension-6 conundrum".

(b) Continuous-variable setting. For a single continuous-variable quantum system (e.g., position/momentum on L^2(ℝ)), the maximum number of mutually unbiased bases (suitably defined via canonical conjugacy) is exactly 3.

(c) Coarse-grained setting. Consider periodic coarse-graining of continuous-variable observables that produces effective d-dimensional measurements, leading to the notion of mutually unbiased measurements (MUMs) in the coarse-grained scenario. In this framework, every even-dimensional coarse-grained system admits at most 3 MUMs (matching the continuous-variable bound), while odd-dimensional coarse-grained systems may admit more.

Problem. Establish or refute a structural relationship between the following two phenomena:
(i) the fact that in the coarse-grained continuous-variable scenario the number of mutually unbiased measurements in even dimensions is bounded by 3 (so that, in particular, dimension 6 is not distinguished from other even dimensions), and
(ii) the open question of whether M(6) = 3 in the discrete Hilbert-space setting.

Specifically: provide a rigorous mathematical link (e.g., a limiting procedure, embedding, or no-go argument) that derives the conjectural bound M(6) ≤ 3 from the even-dimensional coarse-grained bound, or alternatively prove that no such direct connection exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The maximum number of mutually unbiased bases in dimension 6 remains a well-known open problem; only the bound M(6) ≥ 3 is established, with M(6) = 3 conjectured but unproven. Recent reviews (2024) on MUBs in composite dimensions still list this as open. The coarse-grained continuous-variable result showing at most 3 MUMs in even dimensions is established, but no rigorous link between this fact and the discrete dimension-6 conundrum has been demonstrated; the connection remains an open question.

status_evidence.title: Mutually Unbiased Bases in Composite Dimensions – A Review
status_evidence.snippet: d = 6 is the smallest dimension for which the number of mutually unbiased bases is not known.
status_evidence.claim: The dimension-6 MUB problem is still open as of recent reviews.

status_evidence.title: Mutual Unbiasedness in Coarse-Grained Continuous Variables
status_evidence.snippet: Mutual unbiasedness for coarse-grained measurements of continuous variable systems can be established via periodic coarse graining; even-dimensional coarse-grained systems admit at most 3 MUMs.
status_evidence.claim: The even-dimensional coarse-grained bound of 3 MUMs is established, but its relation to discrete N=6 is not proven.

status_evidence.title: The problem of mutually unbiased bases in dimension 6
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of approaches; M(6) remains unknown.
